items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] In a sense I think that those clarinet players, Barney and Noon especially, were part of a family.

ctx.x: Well Hawkins, like Duke, like Louis, a creator. And I always say that the imitators never, never greatest creators. To me Hawkins would always be the number one man. To me. A lot of those would come over and play a lot. A lot of those might blow Louis up. I mean Louis is still the king of that style. He's the creator. Hawkins was the creator of that fine saxophone player. A lot of them got a lot of good ones. But to me Hawkins has always number one. Always will be with Mamey.

In a sense I think that those clarinet players, Barney and Noon especially, were part of a family. In other words they were not especially creators even though they had great originality and you identify them immediately. They're of a family, maybe comes back from Teal. Teal and Bache.

Teal was probably the greatest of the Teal. He laid out in the style. Then Bache came along before he took up that old soprano sax. I never could see why Bache took that dog on soprano sax. Yet he made a whole lot of money with it. Well see people don't, they're lame like that's paying the bills, they don't know anything about what's going on.
